correctness.rationale: All 3^10−1=59048 nonzero ternary cubic coefficient vectors were treated via exact projective incidence on 13 points and 13 lines; 9880 blocking forms. Independent code divided 4940 projective blocking equations into ten exact PGL3(F3) orbits via elementary generators; one orbit of size 936 alone was geometrically smooth, established using affine-patch Groebner unit-ideal tests on one representative of every projective orbit. This gives 1872 smooth blocking forms, one orbit, stabilizer 5616/936=6 and six rational points. Pair/line incidences give t1,t2,t3=(6,3,4). Unlike finite samples, the coefficient/orbit enumeration is exhaustive and geometric smoothness is checked algebraically, avoiding unsupported extension cutoffs. Proof limited to embedded plane cubics over F3.

originality.rationale: Asgarli, Ghioca and Yip already establish existence of the characteristic-three blocking cubic and give the same explicit equation in Example 3.5; neither the existence nor representative alone is original. The distinct surviving theorem is exhaustive classification of *every* smooth blocking ternary cubic into one PGL3(F3) orbit, plus orbit and incidence census. Published blocking-point-set catalogues do not automatically classify cubic equations or their projective stabilizers; small-elliptic finite geometry tables may encode the orbit and remain a risk.
residual_risks: Earlier finite geometry and elliptic-embedding catalogues might implicitly encode the single 936-element orbit.
Only geometrically smooth embedded cubics over F3; not all elliptic isomorphism classes or fields.

value.rationale: A sharp and motivated exceptional case is completely closed: known existence and q>=5 nonexistence do not determine projective uniqueness, number of equations or stabilizer. The exhaustive orbit classification and line-incidence refinement provide reusable exact finite-geometric data.

final_claim: Every geometrically smooth plane cubic over F3 whose rational points meet every F3-line is projectively equivalent to Y^2Z-X^3-X^2Z+XZ^2=0; exactly 936 projective equations, 1872 nonzero forms, stabilizer order 6, 6 rational points and line frequencies 6,3,4.
limitations: All polynomial equations are over F3 and smooth over algebraic closure; only projective equivalence as embedded curves.
Enumeration and Groebner checks have not been formally verified in a proof assistant.
